title: Is $60 Billion Enough to Save Ukraine?

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson, and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档关于设计之爱及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 即使是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店做 DJ 时，你每晚也要带着 300 件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，然后你把 DJ 台

sentences.en: into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成了一个鲜活的、临时搭建的博物馆，里面陈列着精美的 50 年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼带来的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi, and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Late last night, a long-delayed aid package for Ukraine passed its final hurdle in Congress, throwing the embattled country a $60 billion lifeline.
sentences.zh: 昨晚深夜，一项拖延已久的援乌法案在国会通过了最后一道关卡，为这个饱受战争蹂躏的国家提供了 600 亿美元的救命钱。

sentences.en: But given Ukraine's desperation on the battlefield, will that be enough to save it?
sentences.zh: 但考虑到乌克兰在战场上的绝望处境，这足以拯救它吗？

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Mark Santora explains.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事马克·桑托拉将为您解读。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, April 24th.
sentences.zh: 今天是 4 月 24 日，星期三。

sentences.en: So, Mark, last night, after many, many months, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 那么，马克，昨晚，在经历了漫长的数月之后，美国

sentences.en: Congress finally approved an aid package to Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 国会终于批准了一项对乌克兰的援助计划。

sentences.en: It passed in the Senate just before 10 p.m.
sentences.zh: 它在晚上 10 点前在参议院获得通过。

sentences.en: And, of course, it's very, very substantial, billions and billions of dollars.
sentences.zh: 当然，这笔金额非常非常巨大，高达数百亿美元。

sentences.en: But we also know that the war is not going well at all for the Ukrainians right now.
sentences.zh: 但我们也知道，目前乌克兰的战争形势非常不乐观。

sentences.en: You've been in Ukraine covering this war since the beginning in 2022.
sentences.zh: 自 2022 年战争开始以来，你一直身处乌克兰报道这场战争。

sentences.en: You're in Kiev right now.
sentences.zh: 你现在就在基辅。

sentences.en: So my question for you is this.
sentences.zh: 所以我有一个问题想问你。

sentences.en: What does all of this money mean for Ukraine at this point in the war?
sentences.zh: 在战争的这个阶段，所有这些资金对乌克兰意味着什么？

sentences.en: Is it going to make a difference given the state of things?
sentences.zh: 考虑到目前的状况，这会有所改变吗？

sentences.en: 100% it's going to make a difference.
sentences.zh: 百分之百会有所改变。

sentences.en: And the Ukrainians have been waiting for months and months for this news.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰人已经为这个消息等待了数月之久。

sentences.en: $60 billion, of which $46 billion is military aid, basically is the equivalent of all that the United States has given Ukraine over the past two years in total.
sentences.zh: 600 亿美元，其中 460 亿美元是军事援助，这基本上相当于美国过去两年总共给予乌克兰的援助总额。

sentences.en: So it's a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一大笔钱。

sentences.en: It's a lot of supplies.
sentences.zh: 这是大量的物资。

sentences.en: It can buy a lot of what Ukraine needs.
sentences.zh: 它可以买到很多乌克兰急需的东西。

sentences.en: But they need it right now because the situation across the front has been turning increasingly grim for the Ukrainians who find themselves outmanned and outgunned.
sentences.zh: 但他们现在就需要，因为整个前线的局势对乌克兰人来说正变得越来越严峻，他们发现自己人手不足，火力也处于劣势。

sentences.en: So on that point, Mark, it's been a couple of months now since we last talked about the war on the show.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，马克，距离我们上次在节目中讨论这场战争已经过去几个月了。

sentences.en: And, you know, I've been reading your coverage, our colleagues' coverage, and it looks like a very desperate situation for the Ukrainians.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我一直在阅读你的报道，还有我们同事的报道，看起来乌克兰人的处境非常绝望。

sentences.en: Remind us why that is.
sentences.zh: 提醒我们一下这是为什么。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So first of all, if we just step back a little.
sentences.zh: 首先，如果我们稍微回顾一下。

sentences.en: First year of the war was one that started with shock at the breadth of what Russia was trying to do, invade and capture a nation of 40 million people, the largest in Europe.
sentences.zh: 战争的第一年，人们对俄罗斯试图做的事情感到震惊，即入侵并占领一个拥有 4000 万人口的国家，这是欧洲最大的国家。

sentences.en: And then it was about Russian failure and Ukrainian success in pushing back that invasion, first protecting the capital, then reclaiming like 50% of the country.
sentences.zh: 然后是俄罗斯的失败和乌克兰在击退入侵方面的成功，先是保卫了首都，然后收复了约 50% 的国土。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That was the David and Goliath story.
sentences.zh: 那是大卫与歌利亚的故事。

sentences.en: That was year one.
sentences.zh: 那是第一年。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And I think Ukraine surprised the world.
sentences.zh: 我认为乌克兰让世界感到惊讶。

sentences.en: They surprised the Kremlin.
sentences.zh: 他们让克里姆林宫感到惊讶。

sentences.en: And maybe even they surprised themselves a bit.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能连他们自己也感到有些惊讶。

sentences.en: But the year ended on sort of this optimistic note that Ukraine can not just hold their own, but they can take the fight to the Russians.
sentences.zh: 但这一年以一种乐观的基调结束，即乌克兰不仅能守住阵地，还能主动向俄罗斯人发起反击。

sentences.en: And then we get to year two.
sentences.zh: 然后我们进入了第二年。

sentences.en: And year two is this year of ghastly violence, but very little change along the front lines.
sentences.zh: 第二年是可怕暴力的一年，但前线几乎没有什么变化。

sentences.en: Russia tries to do an offensive.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯试图发动进攻。

sentences.en: They fail.
sentences.zh: 他们失败了。

sentences.en: Ukraine tries to do an offensive.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰试图发动进攻。

sentences.en: They fail.
sentences.zh: 他们也失败了。

sentences.en: Russia, again, they try and gain more land and largely fail.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯再次试图获得更多土地，但基本上都失败了。

sentences.en: So you have this sort of back and forth going on.
sentences.zh: 所以你看到的是这种来回拉锯的局面。

sentences.en: But at the end of year two, something changes.
sentences.zh: 但在第二年结束时，情况发生了变化。

sentences.en: For the first time in the course of the war,
sentences.zh: 在战争过程中，这是第一次，

sentences.en: USAID first slows, and then it basically stops.
sentences.zh: 美国援助先是放缓，然后基本上停止了。

sentences.en: So as we get into year three now, we see the Ukrainians, they're not just stuck, but they're basically fighting to hold on for dear life.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们现在进入第三年时，我们看到乌克兰人不仅陷入了困境，而且基本上是在拼命挣扎以求生存。

sentences.en: And what does it look like right now to be holding on for dear life?
sentences.zh: 现在这种“拼命挣扎以求生存”是什么样子的？

sentences.en: Describe that for us.
sentences.zh: 请为我们描述一下。

sentences.en: So, Sabrina, there are three main challenges.
sentences.zh: 萨布丽娜，主要有三个挑战。

sentences.en: And the first, most critical, and probably the most obvious, is a shortage of weapons and ammunition for those weapons.
sentences.zh: 第一个，也是最关键的，可能也是最明显的，就是武器和弹药的短缺。

sentences.en: It's pretty simple in war.
sentences.zh: 战争其实很简单。

sentences.en: The side that can't shoot back generally loses.
sentences.zh: 无法还击的一方通常会输。

sentences.en: And when we would go on visits to the front line over the course of the winter and then into the spring here, what we found were commanders who were rationing their shells.
sentences.zh: 当我们整个冬天以及进入春天去前线访问时，我们发现指挥官们都在定量配给炮弹。

sentences.en: They had maybe one for every three Russian shells in the late winter.
sentences.zh: 在冬末，他们可能每发射三枚俄罗斯炮弹才能还击一枚。

sentences.en: And then it went to one for every five Russian shells.
sentences.zh: 后来变成了每五枚俄罗斯炮弹还击一枚。

sentences.en: And more recently, it's one to ten.
sentences.zh: 最近，比例变成了一比十。

sentences.en: So they found themselves, you know, not just in a position of being outgunned, but outgunned to such a degree that they might have to fall back.
sentences.zh: 所以他们发现自己不仅处于火力劣势，而且劣势大到可能不得不撤退。

sentences.en: Simply put, running out of bullets.
sentences.zh: 简单来说，就是子弹快用完了。

sentences.en: Which is the most basic building block of war.
sentences.zh: 这是战争最基本的要素。

sentences.en: Yeah, and this war in particular,
sentences.zh: 是的，特别是这场战争，

sentences.en: 80% of the deaths have been from direct fire, from artillery and rockets.
sentences.zh: 80% 的死亡是由直接火力造成的，来自火炮和火箭弹。

sentences.en: And the way the Russians fight, sending wave after wave of soldiers to attack Ukrainian trenches and fortifications, the main way you stop these waves of attacks
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人的作战方式是派遣一波又一波的士兵去攻击乌克兰的战壕和防御工事，阻止这些攻击浪潮的主要方法

sentences.en: is kill as many of the attackers as you can.
sentences.zh: 就是尽可能多地消灭进攻者。

sentences.en: And without artillery, you simply can't kill enough people.
sentences.zh: 如果没有火炮，你根本无法消灭足够多的人。

sentences.en: And so eventually their positions will become overrun and they'll have to fall back.
sentences.zh: 所以最终他们的阵地会被攻破，他们将不得不撤退。

sentences.en: And in the past couple months, we've started to really see that and the impact it's having on the battlefield as Ukraine loses territory.
sentences.zh: 在过去几个月里，我们开始真正看到这一点，以及它对战场的影响，因为乌克兰正在失去领土。

sentences.en: Okay, so that's artillery.
sentences.zh: 好的，那是火炮的问题。

sentences.en: What else?
sentences.zh: 还有什么？

sentences.en: What I think almost every Ukrainian would tell you what they desperately need are air defense systems and the munitions that make those systems work.
sentences.zh: 我认为几乎每个乌克兰人都会告诉你，他们迫切需要的是防空系统以及让这些系统发挥作用的弹药。

sentences.en: So when we're talking about air defense systems, we're talking about a whole range of stuff from basically guys on the back of pickup trucks with machine guns
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论防空系统时，我们指的是各种各样的东西，从基本上是坐在皮卡车后座、手持机枪

sentences.en: who are searching for Russian drones in the sky to the most sophisticated air defense systems that only America can provide, which are called the Patriot batteries.
sentences.zh: 搜寻天空中俄罗斯无人机的人，到只有美国才能提供的最先进的防空系统，也就是“爱国者”导弹系统。

sentences.en: So Russia's most sophisticated missiles fly like 10 times the speed of sound.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯最先进的导弹飞行速度大约是音速的 10 倍。

sentences.en: That's where you need something like the Patriot.
sentences.zh: 这就是你需要像“爱国者”这样的东西的地方。

sentences.en: And these are the only thing Ukraine has really that can shoot down Russian ballistic missiles.
sentences.zh: 这些是乌克兰真正拥有的唯一能击落俄罗斯弹道导弹的东西。

sentences.en: So these are like defending the skies, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上是在保卫天空。

sentences.en: Like, it's very, very dangerous to not have them.
sentences.zh: 没有它们会非常非常危险。

sentences.en: It's not just dangerous for the people in the cities and towns.
sentences.zh: 这不仅对城市和城镇中的人们来说很危险。

sentences.en: It's really dangerous for the troops on the front line because the other thing air defense systems give you is it prevents or at least it deters
sentences.zh: 对前线的部队来说更是极其危险，因为防空系统提供的另一件事是，它阻止或至少威慑了

sentences.en: Russian fighter pilots from flying into the area where these things are operating.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯战斗机飞行员飞入这些系统运作的区域。

sentences.en: So once these air defenses basically ran out,
sentences.zh: 所以一旦这些防空系统基本上耗尽，

sentences.en: Russian fighter bombers are now basically strafing the front line, flying closer and closer and dropping these massive bombs onto Ukrainian fortifications
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯战斗轰炸机现在基本上是在前线进行扫射，飞得越来越近，将这些巨大的炸弹投向乌克兰的防御工事，

sentences.en: and also some of these towns and cities that had been out of range of Russian artillery.
sentences.zh: 以及一些原本在俄罗斯火炮射程之外的城镇和城市。

sentences.en: And Mark, what are we seeing as a result of Ukraine being kind of naked in the sky like this?
sentences.zh: 马克，由于乌克兰在空中变得如此“赤裸”，我们看到了什么结果？

sentences.en: Well, on the front, it's opened up this whole new challenge because it's allowed Russian warplanes to basically dip into Russia's almost limitless stock
sentences.zh: 嗯，在前线，这开启了一个全新的挑战，因为它让俄罗斯战机能够利用俄罗斯几乎无限的库存，

sentences.en: of one ton, two ton big bombs that were built ages ago, but that they can strap wings to and guidance systems and obliterate Ukrainian fortifications.
sentences.zh: 那些很久以前制造的 1 吨、2 吨重的大炸弹，他们可以给这些炸弹装上机翼和制导系统，从而摧毁乌克兰的防御工事。

sentences.en: I mean, I'll just tell you personally, you know, whenever you go into a combat zone, it's the noise that strikes you firSt.
sentences.zh: 我个人可以告诉你，你知道，每当你进入战区，首先冲击你的是噪音。

sentences.en: But the first time I heard these things, it shocked me.
sentences.zh: 但我第一次听到这些东西时，我被震惊了。

sentences.en: We were outside Avdivka, maybe two miles away, and you just heard this thunder.
sentences.zh: 我们在阿夫迪夫卡外面，大约两英里远的地方，你只听到了这种雷鸣声。

sentences.en: And Russia was dropping at the peak of the battle for Avdivka, something like 250 of these in 48 hours, each of them weighing and loaded with more than one ton of explosives.
sentences.zh: 在阿夫迪夫卡战役最激烈的时候，俄罗斯在 48 小时内投下了大约 250 枚这种炸弹，每一枚都重达一吨以上，装满了炸药。

sentences.en: It's really hard to get your head around just how big this is.
sentences.zh: 真的很难想象这到底有多大。

sentences.en: So the introduction of these in mass along the front has really changed the dynamic and presented all kinds of problems for the Ukrainians.
sentences.zh: 因此，在前线大规模引入这些武器确实改变了态势，并给乌克兰人带来了各种各样的问题。

sentences.en: Avdivka, of course, being the town that Russia took this winter after practically obliterating it.
sentences.zh: 阿夫迪夫卡当然就是俄罗斯在几乎将其夷为平地后，于今年冬天占领的那个城镇。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so then when you take this all together, the introduction of these heavy bombs, the lack of defenses against ballistic missiles, what you see is it's starting to take
sentences.zh: 所以当你把这一切加在一起，引入这些重型炸弹，缺乏针对弹道导弹的防御，你所看到的是它开始对

sentences.en: a growing toll on civilians as well.
sentences.zh: 平民造成越来越大的伤亡。

sentences.en: The UN estimated that in March, we saw a 20% increase in the number of civilian deaths compared to just the month before.
sentences.zh: 联合国估计，与上个月相比，3 月份的平民死亡人数增加了 20%。

sentences.en: And they attributed that mostly to widespread and more successful Russian aerial strikes.
sentences.zh: 他们将此主要归因于俄罗斯广泛且更成功的空中打击。

sentences.en: So this is really just a disaster for Ukraine, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这对乌克兰来说真的是一场灾难，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it's running out of almost everything.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它几乎什么都快用完了。

sentences.en: And this has put it in kind of a defensive crouch.
sentences.zh: 这使它陷入了一种防御性的窘境。

sentences.en: It's really a complete turnaround from where it was at the beginning of the war.
sentences.zh: 这与战争初期的情况相比，确实是一个彻底的转变。

sentences.en: What's the second challenge Ukraine has been dealing with?
sentences.zh: 乌克兰一直在处理的第二个挑战是什么？

sentences.en: Well, this is a challenge that affects really the entire country.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个真正影响整个国家的挑战。

sentences.en: And that has to do with the power grid.
sentences.zh: 这与电网有关。

sentences.en: The ability of Russia to target and target successfully a number of key Ukrainian power-generating facilities has had a devastating impact on Ukraine's ability to supply power,
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯瞄准并成功打击了许多关键的乌克兰发电设施，这对乌克兰的供电能力造成了毁灭性的影响，

sentences.en: particularly in the eaSt.
sentences.zh: 特别是在东部地区。

sentences.en: We just came back from Kharkiv in eastern Ukraine, where Russia has completely destroyed every single thermal power plant the city had to produce its own power.
sentences.zh: 我们刚从乌克兰东部的哈尔科夫回来，俄罗斯在那里彻底摧毁了该市所有用于自主发电的热电厂。

sentences.en: So it's basically trying to bring power from across the country to provide at least a minimal level of energy for critical infrastructure like water and sewage.
sentences.zh: 所以它基本上是在试图从全国各地输送电力，以提供至少最低限度的能源，用于水和污水处理等关键基础设施。

sentences.en: And people have, you know, sometimes as little as two, three hours of power a day.
sentences.zh: 人们有时每天只有两三个小时的电力供应。

sentences.en: And then if you just, you know, pull back a bit, you look across the country.
sentences.zh: 如果你稍微退后一步，看看全国各地。

sentences.en: And I met with the head of one of the major power utilities here who said that these strikes, starting on March 22nd, really, have been more successful
sentences.zh: 我见过这里一家主要电力公司的负责人，他说从 3 月 22 日开始的这些打击，确实比战争第一个冬天发生的打击更成功，

sentences.en: and done more damage to the Ukrainian power grid than even the strikes that occurred in the first winter of war, which, if you remember, Sabrina, those almost took down the grid
sentences.zh: 对乌克兰电网造成的破坏也更大。萨布丽娜，如果你还记得的话，那次打击差点让电网瘫痪，

sentences.en: and caused the country to go into a blackout.
sentences.zh: 并导致全国陷入停电。

sentences.en: So Ukraine is in a really tough spot when it comes to power generation.
sentences.zh: 所以乌克兰在发电方面处于非常困难的境地。

sentences.en: So this all adds up to a pretty serious problem for Ukraine, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这一切加起来对乌克兰来说是一个相当严重的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, lack of electricity can really cripple a country's economy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，缺乏电力真的会瘫痪一个国家的经济。

sentences.en: Absolutely, Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样，萨布丽娜。

sentences.en: And, you know, these power outages, they affect civilians across the country,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这些停电影响了全国的平民，

sentences.en: which brings us to probably our third biggest challenge for Ukraine, which is people.
sentences.zh: 这把我们带到了乌克兰可能面临的第三大挑战，那就是人力。

sentences.en: They need soldiers.
sentences.zh: 他们需要士兵。

sentences.en: And this is by all accounts the deadliest war since the end of the Second World War.
